passages.title: The Lost Key
sentences: Ben and Ana got off the bus after school.
Ben looked in his bag for the house key.
The key was gone.
Ben frowned and looked in every pocket.
Ana went back to the bus stop.
She looked under the bench.
Then she held up a shiny key.
Ben grinned.
"Thank you!" he said.

passages.title: The Rover Ramp
sentences: Priya brought her rover to the robot fair at Harbor Middle School.
Her job was to drive it up a steep wooden ramp.
The rover rolled halfway up and then stopped.
Its battery was empty.
Priya groaned and put her hands on her head.
She had worked on the rover for three weeks.
She found a charger and plugged the rover in.
While she waited, she checked every wire.
Twenty minutes later, she tried again.
This time the rover climbed all the way to the top.
Priya smiled at Ms. Ortiz.
She had fixed it all by herself.

passages.title: The Milkmaid and Her Pail
sentences: A farm girl walked to market with a pail of milk on her head.
As she walked, she made plans.
"I will sell this milk and buy some eggs," she thought.
"The eggs will hatch into chickens."
"I will sell the chickens and buy a new blue dress."
She smiled and gave a happy little skip.
She pictured the dress and tossed her head with pride.
The pail tipped over.
All the milk spilled onto the dusty road.
The girl looked at the empty pail.
Her eggs, her chickens and her new dress were all gone.
Tears came to her eyes.

credit.title: The Milkmaid and Her Pail
credit.author: Aesop, retold for Wayfinder

passages.title: Maya's Comic
sentences: The library put up a comic show, and Maya's comic was on the wall.
It was about a rock that rolled all the way down Lantern Peaks.
On the first day of the show, Maya stood at the back of the room.
Her hands felt cold, and her stomach felt tight.
This was the first time strangers would see her drawings.
What if they thought her comic was boring?
A boy of about eight stopped in front of it.
He read every box, and then he laughed out loud at the last one.
"The rock does a flip into the creek!" he told his dad.
Then he turned around and saw Maya's name tag.
"Did you draw that?" he asked. "Can you sign my map of the show?"
Maya signed her name in big letters.
She smiled the whole way home.
That night, she drew three new comics.

passages.title: The Old Oak
sentences: For many years, a giant oak tree stood in the middle of Harbor Park.
Sam and his friends met under it after school.
Pixel liked to nap in its shade.
But the tree was very old, and its trunk was soft and weak inside.
Workers from the town said it had to come down.
On Monday, workers cut the tree down.
Sam stood by the fence and looked at the empty spot.
His eyes filled with tears.
He would miss the shade and the bumpy roots where he sat.
On Saturday, Grandma Rose came to the park with a small oak in a pot.
Sam, Priya and Leo dug a hole and planted it in the same spot.
Sam patted the soil flat.
"One day, this tree will be big too," he said, and he smiled.

steps.say: The question asks why Ben grinned. First I find where he grins.
A feeling often comes right after something happens. So I read the sentence just before.
Ana held up a shiny key.
Earlier, Ben's key was gone. So this is the key he was looking for.
Ben grinned because Ana found his key.
